$comment: The supertall case, and the only building that exercises double-deck cars. Eight double-deck shuttles connect a two-level ground lobby to three two-level sky lobbies; six local zones hang off those lobbies. Deck assignment is a real decision here, not a formality: zone 3 is anchored to sky lobby level 26 and zone 4 to level 27, so the deck a sky-lobby-bound passenger boards is dictated by where they are going, while zones 5 and 6 board from either level and turn deck choice into pure load balancing. The two low zones open at both ground lobby levels, so every populated floor is reachable from the street entrance and no arrival is ever stranded on a lobby level it cannot leave. Most deferrable building in the set - see docs/04-test-buildings.md.

transportModes.$comment: The escalator pair a real two-level double-deck lobby uses to move people between its two levels. Traversal time is DERIVED, not quoted: rise 4.5 m (G at 0.0 m, floor 2 at 4.5 m); inclination 30 degrees, which BS EN 115-1 makes the only permitted angle above a 6 m rise and which is the common commercial compromise below it; nominal speed 0.5 m/s, the common commercial nominal speed (EN 115-1 permits up to 0.75 m/s at 30 degrees). Incline length = 4.5 / sin 30 = 9.00 m, so 18.0 s on the incline. EN 115-1 requires at least 2 flat steps at each landing for a rise of 6 m or less, and the standard step depth is 0.40 m, so 2 x 2 x 0.40 = 1.60 m of horizontal run at nominal speed adds 3.2 s. Total landing to landing 21.2 s. No CIBSE Guide D lumped escalator traversal figure was available to check this against; see docs/02-elevator-reference.md.
transportModes.name: Ground lobby escalator pair (G <-> 2)

notes: Double-deck geometry: each shuttle car has two decks 4.5 m apart, and every entry in servesFloorPairs is a pair of floors exactly 4.5 m apart - [G, 2] at 0.0/4.5, [26, 27] at 105.6/110.1, [51, 52] at 211.2/215.7, [76, 77] at 303.0/307.5. The lower deck serves the first floor of each pair, the upper deck the second, and both decks open simultaneously. A loader should assert that constraint; if a floor pair does not match deckSeparationM the configuration is physically impossible.

Deck assignment is binding at sky lobby A and free at sky lobbies B and C, which puts both halves of the double-deck problem in one building. Zone 3 boards only at 26 (lower deck) and zone 4 only at 27 (upper deck), so a passenger for floor 45 who is put on the lower deck lands at 26 and cannot reach zone 4 from there: the shuttle group must pair each call to the deck that matches the destination zone. Zones 5 and 6 board from either level of their sky lobby, so their deck choice is pure load balancing between the decks.

Every origin/destination pair has a declared route. It used to be an all-elevator route, because the schema had no way to declare anything else: the note this replaces said so, and said that demand which silently cannot be served is worse than a slightly generous shaft layout. That is still true, and the schema now has transportModes. The G <-> 2 crossing is the ground lobby escalator, which is what a real double-height lobby uses, and it is no longer charged to zone-1-local or zone-2-local as a one-floor elevator leg - 292 of this building's 3,549 lift legs at seed 20260726 were exactly that hop, and now none of them is (DECISIONS.md, and traffic/transportRoute.test.ts). The routes are therefore: G -> 3-14 and G -> 15-25 direct; G -> lower deck -> 26 -> zone 3; G -> escalator -> 2 -> upper deck -> 27 -> zone 4; either deck -> 51/52 -> zone 5 and 76/77 -> zone 6. Cross-zone interfloor works the same way in reverse, e.g. 30 -> 45 is zone-3-local 30->26, lower deck 26->G, escalator G->2, upper deck 2->27, zone-4-local 27->45. Note what that last one shows: the three sky lobby pairs (26/27, 51/52, 76/77) declare NO escalator, so a cross-lobby interfloor passenger still rides all the way down to the ground lobby to change decks. Whether those pairs should also be joined is a live question about this building; nothing in core prevents it. zone-1-local and zone-2-local still open at both G and 2, which is what a real double-height ground lobby does with its low-zone shafts, and that is what keeps zones 1 and 2 reachable from both levels - before that, zone 2 was reachable only from floor 2 and zone 1 only from G, so roughly half of all arrivals for those two zones, 2,015 occupants between them, had no route at all.

Only G is an entrance. Floor 2 is the upper level of the same double-height lobby, not a second street entrance: flagging both would split incoming demand across two lobby levels with nothing in the data to weight the split, and the split would silently decide how much traffic starts on the wrong side of the deck pairing. All eight lobby floors (G, 2, 26, 27, 51, 52, 76, 77) are flagged isTransferFloor, so a journey that changes banks at any of them stays one journey and time-to-destination spans every leg. Ground lobbies are not implicitly transfer-capable - the flag is declared, not inferred from isEntrance - and the same is done in mixed-use-high-rise and secure-tower.

Lobby levels carry zero resident population on purpose. All of their demand is transfer traffic re-injected from the leg that just arrived, so any transfer accounting bug shows up here as arrivals appearing from nowhere or journeys that never complete. Two legs per journey above floor 25, three when the destination zone is anchored to the far lobby level.

Six service zones, tapering upward the way a real supertall does: dense office plates low (90 and 85 per floor over 4.2 m floors) get narrow 11-12 floor zones, sparse hotel (36 per floor, 3.6 m) and residential (22 per floor, 3.4 m) get wide 23 floor zones. Total 4,887 occupants over a 386.8 m rise. Traffic profile is overridden per range: office-standard below 51, hotel 53-75, residential 78-100.

The per-range trafficProfile overrides carry the same open question as mixed-use-high-rise. The config module defines a floor's override as governing demand originating on that floor, so 'hotel' governs the 40% outgoing and 20% interfloor components of 53-75 and 'residential' the 75% outgoing and 10% interfloor of 78-100. The incoming component of each originates at G, and the rule for attributing an entrance-origin leg to its destination floor's profile is not yet declared anywhere. Hotel is near-symmetric (40/40/20) so the choice barely moves zone 5; residential is not, so zone 6 results should be read as the morning down-peak that 'residential' (governingPeak down-peak-am) actually describes. There is no time-of-day or scenario selector in the building schema; an evening case needs a declared profile in traffic-profiles.json, selected through the same override field.

Capacity sizing, roughly 80-88% of up-peak handling capacity per bank: zone 1 1,080 occupants on 5 cars, zone 2 935 on 5, zone 3 770 on 4, zone 4 768 on 4, zone 5 828 on 6 (hotel transfer time is 1.5 s, and two-way hotel traffic is less efficient than one-way office traffic), zone 6 506 on 3. The eight shuttles move about 320 passengers per 5 minutes against a combined above-lobby peak near 250, so the shuttle group has headroom - the interesting queue forms at the sky lobbies during the return leg, not at the ground lobby.

10 m/s shuttles reach rated speed on the G to 76 run (303 m) but barely hold it on G to 26 (105.6 m), where roughly 90 m of the trip is acceleration and deceleration. Any conclusion about shuttle speed drawn without the jerk-limited profile will be wrong for the lower sky lobby and right for the upper one, which is exactly the trap docs/00-project-brief.md warns about.

Per-deck capacity: ratedLoadLbPerDeck 2000 gives 2000/150 = 13 persons per deck, inside the [12, 14] doubleDeckPersonsPerDeck band the ultra-high-speed class declares in data/elevator-specs.json, and the loader cross-checks exactly that. The whole-car ratedLoadLb of 4000 is the sum of the two decks and must never be divided by 150 to obtain a per-deck figure - that yields 26 per deck, 53 per car, and doubles this building's shuttle handling capacity, which would invalidate the sky-lobby contention result the building exists to produce. data/buildings/README.md currently states the wrong form of that rule; the loader implements the right one.

Fields doubleDeck, deckSeparationM, ratedLoadLbPerDeck, servesFloorPairs, isTransferFloor and the per-floor trafficProfile override are declared in packages/core/src/config/schema.ts and documented in data/buildings/README.md. This building is the most deferrable in the set; the other four cover the algorithmic ground without a double-deck model.

Passenger transfer time is declared per car, not inherited from the building type. There is no 'mixed-use' row in elevator-specs.json -> timing.passengerTransferS on purpose, because this tower's zones serve three populations that load at different speeds. Zones 1-4 are office and declare 1.2 s; zone 5 is hotel and declares 1.5 s (which is also what the capacity-sizing note above already assumed); zone 6 is residential and declares 1.75 s (ISO 4190-6). The double-deck shuttles declare 1.75 s because they feed every zone above the lobby including the residential one, and understating tp understates the round trip - the optimistic direction. Before this was declared, every car in this building silently ran at the 1.2 s office default, including the residential zone.
